extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was manually collected by a team of over 50 college students (including co-authors) from various disciplines, who gathered multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, and created new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, lecture materials, and online sources.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students and co-authors specializing in relevant majors collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, creating new questions where necessary, and annotated fields including the question, answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors, problems were distributed among different co-authors for format and typo checking, and authors categorized the problems into four difficulty levels. A secondary review team also vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI is of societal importance due to the significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption associated with AI systems reaching the substitution threshold for human labor.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning; developing next-generation multimodal foundation models; monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning involved three stages: first, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify and eliminate duplicate problems; second, problems were checked for format and typos to ensure adherence to a standardized format; third, approximately 10% of the problems were filtered out and excluded from the benchmark for being classified as very easy.
